correctness.rationale: The two explicit Cayley/rook neighbor constructions each have 16 degree-6 vertices and exactly 2 common neighbors for each pair, yielding A²=4I+2J and the same spectrum 6,2^6,(-2)^9. Rook row/column K4 gives eight four-one fixed majority configurations; Shrikhande neighborhood C6 precludes any K4. Independently built all six neighbor masks and enumerated all 2^16 bit states for each graph, traced complete functional graphs until cycle repetition, and classified exact first-entry time tau and least period. Rook p=1 tau=0:302,1:10104,2:29984,3:18720; p=2 tau=0:2394,1:4032. Shrikhande p=1 tau=0:142,1:7576,2:26240,3:18496,4:9024,5:960; p=2 tau=0:1370,1:1728. Each graph totals 65536; primitive two-cycle orbits 2394/2=1197 and 1370/2=685. The enumeration is exhaustive finite proof exactly over each declared 16-vertex graph; it asserts nothing for arbitrary strongly regular graphs or other tie conventions.

evidence: Four-cube Q4 majority has 702 fixed points and 885 primitive two-cycles, distinct underlying 16-vertex graph.

originality.rationale: The fundamental eventual-period-at-most-two theorem is classical, but it supplies no exact two-graph census, transient depth or 8-versus-0 fixed-point witness. Related published exhaustive censuses on the same Shrikhande/rook graph pair use a three-state excitation automaton, whereas the same-rule census on Q4 uses a different graph. Both potential ambiguities were checked at the actual rule level.
